key_insight: A dual-layer pipeline combining LLM-based screening with expert educator review can efficiently generate and validate synthetic musculoskeletal cases for health professional education.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help create scalable, privacy-preserving teaching cases, but human review is still needed to catch subtle clinical inaccuracies and contextual gaps.
method: Generated 128 synthetic MSK cases across 28 conditions using GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Llama 4 Scout.
Ran automated LLM-as-judge screening for alignment, JSON correctness, relevance, bias, toxicity, and completeness.
Had four MSK physiotherapy educators rate the surviving cases on accuracy, realism, fidelity, relevance, and usability.
evidence_signal: Ninety cases passed automated screening; GPT-4.1 had the highest pass rate (96%) and strongest expert scores, while expert ratings showed high validity for usability, relevance, and realism.
watch_item: Automated metrics only weakly matched some expert judgments, so reliance on LLM screening alone could miss clinically important errors.
paper_title: PhysiCase: Development and dual-layer validation of synthetic cases for health professional education: A pilot study leveraging Generative AI
